title: The Strokes at Red Rocks
description: Basecamp tip from The Trailhead: this is the two-night Strokes stand at the greatest natural amphitheatre on the planet, with Hamilton Leithauser and OLUM opening. Bring a layer even in July — the moment the sun drops behind the sandstone monoliths, the mountain air turns cool, and the altitude means one drink hits like two. Arrive early to walk the ridge before the set.
pin_ticker: Strokes take the Rocks — two nights only

title: Darius Rucker with Old Crow Medicine Show
description: The Trailhead says: a Saturday-night singalong under the stars with Darius Rucker, Old Crow Medicine Show, and Austin Williams. This is the quintessential Red Rocks summer bill — roots, twang, and a crowd that knows every word. Pack water; you're at 6,450 feet and the climb from the lower lot is real, but the payoff is the best seat in Colorado.
pin_ticker: Darius Rucker — Saturday under the sandstone

title: Nathaniel Rateliff with the Colorado Symphony
description: A hometown moment worth planning a trip around: Denver's own Nathaniel Rateliff backed by the full Colorado Symphony, on the Rocks. The Trailhead's read — this is the emotional high point of the season, strings swelling against the red stone at dusk. Nights in August still dip cool up here, so a fleece and a flask of something warm are your friends.
pin_ticker: Rateliff + the Symphony, one Denver night

title: Reggae on the Rocks
description: One of the longest-running reggae festivals in the country, and a Red Rocks institution: Rebelution headlines with Skip Marley, Third World, Etana, MAOLI, and Denver's own Judge Roughneck. The Trailhead calls this the warmest day on the mountain — a full afternoon-to-night lineup, so hydrate hard at altitude, sunscreen up early, and let the bass roll off the sandstone.
pin_ticker: Reggae on the Rocks — all-day riddim at 6,450 ft

title: RiNo First Friday Art Walk
date: recurring: first Friday monthly, 6–9 PM (Aug 7, Sep 4, Oct 2, Nov 6, Dec 4, 2026)
address: Larimer & Walnut Streets, RiNo Art District, Denver, CO 80205
description: This is the beating heart of Denver's mural economy — galleries throw open their doors, muralists work live, food trucks line up, and the whole River North district turns into a walkable open-air show. The Trailhead's route: start on Larimer, arc toward the ArtPark, and trace the same creative current that flows out of Five Points' Welton Street jazz corridor. Free to wander; bring cash for the makers.
pin_ticker: First Friday — RiNo's galleries go loud

title: Union Station Farmers Market
date: recurring: Saturdays 9 AM–1 PM through Oct 23, 2026
description: Saturday mornings, the plaza in front of historic Union Station fills with Colorado growers, ranchers, and bakers. The Trailhead's play: grab a craft coffee, load up on peaches and green chile, then duck inside the Great Hall to people-watch. It's the easiest, most local hour you'll spend in LoDo — and a perfect launchpad before a day exploring downtown.
pin_ticker: Saturday market on the Union Station plaza

title: South Pearl Street Farmers Market
date: recurring: Sundays 9 AM–1 PM through Nov 8, 2026
description: More than 170 vendors line the 1400 and 1500 blocks of South Pearl every Sunday — fresh Colorado produce, just-baked pastries, cut flowers, and chef-worthy bites. The Trailhead pairs it with a Wash Park loop: market first, then a walk or paddle at the park a few blocks north. It's the platonic ideal of a slow Denver Sunday.
pin_ticker: Sunday on South Pearl — 170+ local vendors

title: Great American Beer Festival
description: The biggest name in American beer, and in 2026 it moves outdoors for the first time in its history — more than 1,500 beers from 500-plus breweries under the open Colorado sky at Levitt Pavilion. Sessions run Saturday and Sunday, noon to 4. The Trailhead's altitude warning is dead serious here: samples are small but the mile-high elevation multiplies every pour, so pace yourself and drink water between tastings.

title: Denver Film Festival (49th Annual)
description: For eleven days at the turn of November, Denver becomes a cinema town — hundreds of features, shorts, and music videos screening at the Sie FilmCenter on Colfax and venues across the city. The Trailhead's move: catch an early-evening screening, then walk Colfax for a nightcap. Indoor and warm, it's the perfect pivot as the 300-days-of-sun season starts trading heat for crisp fall nights.
pin_ticker: Denver Film Festival lights up Colfax

title: Denver Christkindlmarket
description: Denver's only authentic German holiday market — timbered stalls, glühwein, hand-carved ornaments, bratwurst, and carols glowing against the winter dark from Nov 20 through Dec 23. The Trailhead's tip: come at dusk when the lights kick on, dress in real layers, and let a hot mug of spiced wine take the mountain chill off. It's the coziest corner of the city all season.

title: Denver Zoo Lights
date: recurring: select nights, late Nov 2026 – early Jan 2027
description: The zoo transforms into a glowing wonderland of millions of lights winding through the animal habitats — a Denver holiday tradition that draws families every December. The Trailhead says bundle up: this is an outdoor walk in real Colorado winter, so hats, gloves, and hot cocoa are non-negotiable. There's an adults-only 21+ night for a quieter, spiked-cider stroll.
pin_ticker: Zoo Lights — a million bulbs after dark

title: National Western Stock Show
description: Sixteen days of pure Western Colorado — championship rodeo, prize livestock, mutton bustin', a downtown kickoff parade with longhorns on the streets, and enough boots and belt buckles to outfit a county. The Trailhead frames it as the deepest-rooted event on the calendar, running Jan 9–24. Dress warm for the barns and grounds; January in Denver swings from bluebird sun to bitter cold in a single afternoon.
pin_ticker: Stock Show — 16 days of rodeo & longhorns
